title: Guide: which crypto wallet should you use?

linkedin.media_title: Which crypto wallet should you use?
linkedin.text:
"Which crypto wallet should I use?" is one of the most common questions I get. Here is the plain-English answer.

First, there are two kinds of wallet. With a custodial wallet, the exchange holds your keys, a bit like money in a bank. With a self-custody wallet, you hold the keys yourself, like cash in your own safe.

Which one, when? If you are holding small amounts and still learning, a regulated exchange is fine. If you are holding for the long term, move it to your own wallet.

Then choose hot or cold. A hot wallet is an app on your phone or browser: easy to use, but always online. A cold wallet is a small hardware device that stays offline and is the hardest to hack.

Set it up safely:
1. Download only from the official website.
2. Write your recovery phrase on paper. Never a screenshot, never the cloud.
3. Send a test amount before moving anything serious.

The three mistakes that cost people the most: sending on the wrong network (same coin, different blockchain, money gone), installing fake wallet apps, and typing their recovery phrase into "sync your wallet" websites. No real wallet will ever ask for it.

Save this for the day you set one up.

Education, not financial advice.
